angles.title: The starter is the whole bakery
angles.thesis: The bread part is really about patience with the slow invisible part of the work, the part that happens before anyone sees anything.

uses.quote: the first month they are not allowed to shape a single loaf
You can't rescue bad fermentation with good scoring.
the failure happened twelve hours before they touched the dough
the patience of reading back through your own records instead of guessing
Not his shaping, not his scoring, the fact that he noticed the starter.
patience with the slow invisible part of the work, the part that happens before anyone sees anything
the bakery one feels like the best story I have heard in months

open_questions: Does the piece stay with the bakery, or reach outward to the reader's own work? The memo states the lesson but not where it lands.

angles.title: Our meeting agenda is upside down
angles.thesis: The thing that needs the whole room gets the least time, so status updates should move to a short written document and the Monday meeting should be only for decisions and disagreements.

uses.quote: half the agenda is status updates that could be a written document
we spent seventy minutes on updates and twenty minutes on the one decision that actually mattered
The thing that needs the whole room gets the least time.
the Monday meeting is only for decisions and disagreements. If there is no decision on the agenda, we cancel the meeting.
Three lines and a link.
the meeting facilitator should change every week
a silent reading start
I want to come back to the meeting one this week because the team needs it

open_questions: Is this addressed to the whole team, or to the managers who "will hate that"? The memo expects the two groups to react differently.

angles.title: Write the toolbox, not the thesis
angles.thesis: The small specific thing is the only way a reader gets in, so an essay should start with one object or one person and let the big idea show up on its own.

uses.quote: I keep stalling because every draft feels too small
I have a feeling, not an argument.
Nobody wrote back to the big abstract ones. So why do I keep starting with the abstract?
But the small specific thing is the only way a reader gets in.
nobody would have read an essay titled inheritance and silence
Write the toolbox, not the thesis.

open_questions: Who is it for: the newsletter's readers, other people who write in public, or the writer as a rule for themselves? The memo doesn't say.

angles.title: The small invisible daily thing

uses.quote: The small invisible daily thing, the starter, the notebook, the toolbox. Maybe that is the actual essay. I don't know yet.
Is it one piece or three pieces? I genuinely can't tell.
the slow invisible part of the work
The toolbox essay was really about inheritance and silence between generations

open_questions: What claim joins the starter, the notebook and the toolbox? The memo names the link but doesn't argue it.
Does the meeting belong in this piece? The memo connects the bakery and the toolbox, but never the meeting.
One piece or three: the writer's own question, still open.
